subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After the authorization-order repair, should plugin-runtime callers be denied patch access to every legacy ownerless session row?
rationale: Failing closed strengthens cross-plugin isolation, but ownerless rows predate this boundary and the change intentionally removes an existing plugin-runtime upgrade path, so repository intent is required.

options.title: Deny ownerless rows
options.body: Keep legacy ownerless sessions operator-only for patching and document and prove that upgrade boundary.

options.title: Migrate safe ownership
options.body: Add an explicit doctor or migration owner that assigns verifiable ownership before plugin-runtime patching is allowed.

options.title: Preserve old access
options.body: Continue allowing ownerless plugin-runtime patches temporarily, accepting weaker isolation until a migration strategy exists.

recommendation.title: Deny ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Keep legacy ownerless sessions operator-only for patching and document and prove that upgrade boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main history connects this person to both the projection accessor ordering and the `sessions.patch` integration point where the policy must be enforced.
